# Measure time accuracy with a nonlinear field

[Fix the grid. Refine the step. Keep the comparison above its floor.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

The [exact vortex](../vorticity/index.qmd) has no advective tendency, so
its exact viscous decay cannot establish nonlinear fourth-order time
accuracy. This retained driver offers a two-mode field whose interactions
do activate the nonlinear stages:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\omega(x,y,0)&=\sin x\sin y\\
&\quad+\tfrac12\sin(2x)\sin(2y).
\end{aligned}
$$

It lives on $[0,2\pi)^2$. Its two Fourier shells have different Laplacian
eigenvalues, so vorticity is not a single constant multiple of its
streamfunction and advection need not vanish.

The separate shear option uses the unit square. The driver keeps those
geometries explicit:

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="setup"}
```

## Keep the viscous part in an integrating factor

For one spectral mode, write $\dot w=Lw+N(w)$ with $L=-\nu|\mathbf k|^2$.
The variable $v=e^{-Lt}w$ satisfies

$$
\dot v=e^{-Lt}N(e^{Lt}v).
$$

Classical RK4 applied to this transformed equation produces four nonlinear
stages. In the implementation, `exp_dt` is $e^{hL}$ and `exp_half` is
$e^{hL/2}$; the final combination is

```{.cpp include="../ns2d/spectral.hpp" snippet="ifrk4_update" dedent=2}
```

The two-thirds state projection also applies before each stage's products.
When $N=0$, only the exact viscous exponential remains. When $L=0$, this
reduces to classical RK4. With both parts active, the nonlinear stages
matter; a stable run alone does not establish their order.

## Compare with one finest-step trajectory

The grid, viscosity, initial field and physical sample times remain fixed.
Only $h$ changes. Let

$$
E(h)=\|\omega_h(T)-\omega_{h_{\mathrm{ref}}}(T)\|_{\mathrm{RMS}}.
$$

The comparison reuses the common-grid Fourier helper from the
[spatial lesson](../spatial-refinement/index.qmd), with equal grid sizes.
There is no spatial rescaling between these trajectories. The reference
is still a finite-step numerical solution, not an exact answer.

For adjacent steps related by a factor two, the reported estimate is

$$
p=\log_2\!\bigl(E(h)/E(h/2)\bigr).
$$

```{.cpp include="../ns2d/temporal_order.hpp" snippet="observed_order"}
```

Choose a factor-of-two ladder when interpreting this helper's `log2`
formula.

The driver withholds a value when either error is at or below the configured
floor, when a row failed, or when the finer comparison is the reference
itself. Its `roundoff` label means that the floor prevented the estimate;
it does not prove that floating point error is the only source of the
small difference. Even above that floor, reference-step error can bias a
ratio. Refine the reference before interpreting a stable estimate as a
method's asymptotic order.

## Run a small nonlinear ladder

From the repository root, with a compatible installed spectral CPU SDK:

```sh
mkdir -p results
openpfc compile examples/flow/temporal-refinement/model.cpp --source-root examples/flow -o results/temporal-refinement
results/temporal-refinement --case two-mode --n 16 --dts 0.2,0.1,0.05,0.025 --times 0.8 --nu 0.05 --outdir results/flow/temporal-refinement
```

Use one MPI rank, as required by this comparison driver. Each step must be
an integer multiple of the finest step. Sample times are rounded to
finest-step indices, and those indices must be divisible by every coarser
subdivision. Choose observation times that are exact multiples of every
step and check the recorded time column.

The [model](model.cpp) uses the shared
[solver](../ns2d/vorticity_stream.hpp),
[spectral operations](../ns2d/spectral.hpp),
[initial fields](../ns2d/cases.hpp),
[comparison helper](../ns2d/band_error.hpp) and
[order helper](../ns2d/temporal_order.hpp). Keep their relative layout when
using downloads; the declared source root captures their quoted includes.
The CMake target remains `ns2d_temporal_refine` at its existing location.
Its original short smoke case and numerical tests are retained.

The supplied small ladder gives the following representative differences
against its finest step:

| $h$ | Vorticity RMS difference | Reported $p$ |
|---:|---:|---:|
| $0.2$ | $1.54\times10^{-7}$ | $3.99$ |
| $0.1$ | $9.69\times10^{-9}$ | $4.08$ |
| $0.05$ | $5.73\times10^{-10}$ | — |
| $0.025$ | Reference | — |

The last comparison is withheld because its finer member is the reference.
A value slightly above four can reflect reference-step bias; it does not
establish a higher-order method.

Read `temporal_errors.csv` and `run.json` under the result directory.
Inspect `status` before interpreting error or order columns. Rows with
nonfinite fields or excessive CFL are recorded as failures; their data
must not be fitted into a convergence line. The table also records mean
drift, divergence, energy differences and the outer-band diagnostic.

Add a finer reference step, keeping the physical times fixed. Then repeat
at a finer grid. The first experiment tests sensitivity to reference time
error; the second asks whether spatial truncation affects the time study.
A two-level smoke test checks execution and output structure, while a
meaningful order estimate needs multiple valid levels above the floor.
